verdict.rationale: Bitwarden's own docs walk through installing and deploying Bitwarden on your own Linux server, and the Public API docs reference a self-hosted instance URL. This confirms first-party self-hosting of the server. However, nothing in the pack shows that every secret stays inside the perimeter: there is no evidence about air-gapped or offline operation, licensing or telemetry calls to Bitwarden's cloud, or data-residency guarantees. Missing for 10: evidence that self-hosted deployments keep all secrets and traffic inside the perimeter (no cloud dependency or call-home), deployment depth beyond a single install-guide line, and independent hands-on corroboration of the official self-hosted server.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can self-host the sync server on my own infrastructure and keep every secret inside my perimeter

citations.quote: This article will walk you through the procedure to install and deploy Bitwarden to your own Linux server.
